A standard, first published in 1983, for how electronic instruments, controllers and computers send performance and control data to each other. It sends instructions such as "play this note" or "turn this knob", not sound.
MIDI/Message — the kinds of messages MIDI sends: MIDI/Note, MIDI/Aftertouch, MIDI/CC, MIDI/Program-Change, MIDI/Pitch-Bend, MIDI/SysEx and MIDI/Clock.
Logseq/Entity/MIDI/Port — the named connections a device presents to a computer.
Pressure on a key or pad after it has gone all the way down, sent as one of two MIDI/Message types.
Polyphonic Key Pressure (A0h–AFh) sends a note number and a pressure value, one stream for each held key.
Channel Pressure (D0h–DFh) sends one pressure value for the whole channel: the greatest pressure among the held keys.
The Launchpad Pro MK3 can send either. Its guide recommends Channel Pressure with Ableton Live (Launchpad/UG/10 Setup/04 Aftertouch Settings).
MPE carries per-note pressure as Channel Pressure by giving each note its own channel.

A bank is a number that a MIDI sender puts in front of a MIDI/Program-Change, so that the program number can mean more than 128 different things. The sender sends it as Bank Select on MIDI/CC 0, CC 32, or both.

The MIDI standard defines the message, but not what the bank number corresponds to. Each instrument that receives it decides that for itself: a block of memory, a variation of a sound, a family of sounds, or nothing at all.
What the instruments below agree on: the bank number waits until a Program Change arrives, and only then does anything change. Yamaha and Roland both state this in their MIDI charts.

A block of memory, chosen with CC 32. The Sequential OB-6 stores 1000 programs in 10 banks of 100. Banks 0–4 hold user programs and 5–9 factory programs. It reads Bank Select from CC 32 only, and a Program Change of 0–99 picks a program inside the bank (OB-6 Operation Manual, Appendix C).

A block of memory, chosen with CC 0 and CC 32 together. The Korg minilogue xd has 500 programs in 5 banks of 100. CC 0 stays at 0, CC 32 picks bank 0–4, and a Program Change of 0–99 picks the program (minilogue xd MIDI Implementation).

A block of memory, chosen with CC 0 alone. The Microfreak has 512 slots in 4 banks of 128: bank 0 is slots 1–128, bank 1 is 129–256, bank 2 is 257–384 and bank 3 is 385–512. Its user guide doesn't describe this; Microfreak/CLI/Upload a preset shows CC 0 = 2 and program 66 selecting slot 323.

A variation of the same instrument sound. On a Roland GS sound module such as the SC-88 Pro, the Program Change picks an instrument, such as piano, and CC 0 picks a variation of it. Bank 0 holds the basic sound and other banks hold variations: CC 0 = 8 with Program Change 2 is Piano 3w, a variation of Piano 3. CC 32 picks which generation's sound set to use (SC-88 Pro Owner's Manual, p. 126 and p. 188).

A family of sounds. On a Yamaha XG module such as the MU50, CC 0 picks the family: 0 for ordinary instruments, 64 for sound effects, and 126 or 127 for drum kits. CC 32 then picks a variation, and the Program Change picks the instrument or kit (MU50 Sound List and MIDI Data).
No banks. The Korg monologue has 100 programs, so a Program Change of 0–99 reaches all of them. Its MIDI chart lists no Bank Select (monologue MIDI Implementation).
Synthesizers and their software also call any named collection a bank, and those collections have nothing to do with Bank Select.

A MIDI/Program-Change tells an instrument to switch to another preset. It carries one number from 0 to 127, so on its own it reaches 128 presets.

A Bank Select message sends a MIDI/Bank number, and the Program Change that follows picks a program under that bank. Together the two numbers can reach many more than 128 sounds. What a bank number corresponds to is up to the receiving instrument: on the MicroFreak it is a block of 128 slots.

Control Change — a MIDI/Message (B0h–BFh) that sets one controller to a value. It carries a controller number and a value, both 0–127.

The controller number names the control: 1 is the modulation wheel, 7 channel volume, 64 the sustain pedal, 74 brightness by default. On/off controllers such as 64 read 63 and below as off, 64 and above as on.
Fine values. Controllers 0–31 can each be paired with 32–63 for the fine half of a 0–16,383 range: 0 Bank Select with 32, 1 Modulation with 33.
RPN and NRPN. Controllers 101 and 100 (RPN) or 99 and 98 (NRPN) pick a parameter, and Data Entry, 6 and 38, sets its value. RPN 0 sets the MIDI/Pitch-Bend range.
Channel mode messages. 120–127 are reserved: All Sound Off (120), Reset All Controllers (121), Local Control (122), All Notes Off (123), Omni Off and On (124, 125), Mono (126) and Poly (127).
The numbers the spec leaves undefined, and so free for custom mappings, are on MIDI/Q/Which-MIDI-CC-numbers-are-free-for-custom-mappings.
In this garden: Microfreak/UG/17 Ext Gear/09 MIDI CC Control, Microfreak/UG/21 Appendix D - CC Values, Launchpad/Custom/Available/1-Arrangement.
The MIDI/Message types that keep devices at one tempo and start and stop them together. They are system real-time messages: they carry no channel and may arrive in the middle of any other message.
Timing Clock (F8h) — sent 24 times per quarter note. The tempo is the spacing between them; the message carries no number.
Start (FAh) plays from the beginning, Stop (FCh) halts, and Continue (FBh) resumes where playback stopped.
Song Position Pointer (F2h), a system common message, tells a follower where to resume, counted in sixteenth notes of six clocks each.

One device sends clock and the others follow. Ableton Live can do either (Ableton/Live/UG/37 Sync with Link Tempo Follower and MIDI/03 Synchronizing via MIDI), and sends clock to the MicroFreak over Microfreak/MIDI/Port/Arturia MicroFreak.
